How do you feel about the story of Kingdom Hearts?

I've only ever played the original Kingdom Hearts, but I thought the story was incredible at the time. (I was a freshman in high school.) It was very complex and intriguing; there were lots of unanswered questions that my friends and I could contemplate. There were secret videos at the end, and secret trailers for upcoming games would come out, and new character designs and Disney worlds would be announced. It was fun to imagine the possibilities, and I even read some fan fiction. (I don't think I ever wrote any, though ...)

Since then, I've followed the stories of the games but haven't played them because I just don't have as much time to play video games as I used to. I like that the story has gotten more complex and has incorporated new characters, but I also feel like it lost its mystery. I remember feeling kind of betrayed when they retconned some of the story elements from the first game and it turned out that Ansem wasn't actually Ansem. I thought the Nobody aspect was a little overwrought; it seemed a little silly that each person was so many different things at once: a heart, a soul, a body, a Nobody, and a Heartless. A lot of the ideas seemed kind of slapdash, and arbitrary and the metaphysical aspects were very vague and muddled (hearts vs. souls, Nobodies vs. Heartless, etc.)

At that point, I realized that the mystery was really just a kind of story hole that a bunch of writers were filling in with their own ideas, not some ethereal world of the imagination (or something like that). In that sense, the story lost of lot of the "magic" and became just a story, although it's still a pretty good one.

As for the future, I think the Birth by Sleep story was interesting and I like the idea that the main characters are now part of a deeper history of Keyblade wielders. It embodies the "coming-of-age" aspect of Kingdom Hearts, because establishing your place in society (and history) is a huge part of becoming an adult. The idea that your life has been largely determined by other people's choices and that your choices will have the same effect on other people is a major realization, and the duties and responsibilities you take on as a result are important.

In terms of weaknesses, I'm glad they're (allegedly) ending the Xehanort saga with KH3 because I'm tired of the same villain.
I never really had a problem with any of it and honestly really liked everything until they involved time traveling.

That definitely changed the feel of the game for me. I felt like it weakened the story because of just how messy the timeline is now. I mean, after lots of reading I understand the plot, but I fear they are over complicating the story without being profound. Like, Primer was initially confusing time-travel movie, but once you understand it you're left with that feeling you get when you solve a tough riddle. You feel a sense of completion and can't help but to look it over again. I don't really feel that way about the Xehanort time travel stuff. I guess we'll see what they do in the next game.

Bitcoin integration into reddit-like social media platforms is the future and the solution to the ad-revenue conundrum that has plagued the internet since its inception. I saw a major announcement from Tesla a couple months ago, stating that they will produce 10 kWh residential-scale energy storage units (batteries) for $3,500. This is (at least according to what I’ve read so far) a 50%+ reduction in cost, which should bring residential-scale (and possibly off the grid, or on only a neighborhood grid) renewable systems to about $0.06-$0.08 per kWh delivered, compared to over $0.10 per kWh in even lower priced US markets. These batteries are available for purchase now, and will begin shipping this summer, so we should soon see it in action.
Home-scale renewable energy production to become lowest cost option?
Now if only we can get the gov't to switch subsidies.

You have to factor in costs of a pretty hefty solar install as well as a nice inverter to actually run all of the AC appliances in the house.

Where a system like this makes decent sense is places that have ridiculous peak electricity rates like California and Hawaii. There you could charge the battery overnight for cheap and then offset your peak rate usage with the stored energy from the battery. This would also help the utility as their peak demand would go down, so they may be more able to meet demand and lower costs a bit.

As far as going totally off grid with renewables, the house, cabin, whatever would have to have a capable system to charge the battery (solar, wind, etc) and then the user would have to figure out if they can reduce their usage to a point that this battery would last long enough. Multiples could be installed to run longer. At a cabin it might not matter if power is totally depleted and there is no wind or sun to charge it back up for a prolonged period. At a residential setting I would think some sort of propane generator could be used to power the house and charge the battery to avoid the whole house going dark.

In an industrial power production sense, they announced a 100kWh battery aimed at producers. This could be used to help meet demand at peak times. And they could charge it for basically free at night. This could reduce peak load rates for consumers potentially. Maybe not to night rates but lower.

As homes and end users get more efficient in their lifestyles (and as tech gets more efficient), its likely battery backup will be pretty commonplace. People seem more comfortable with batteries and not so much with fuel powered generators. Hopefully the batteries are recycled appropriately. Right now I doubt one of those will run a big suburban family home all day with air conditioning, multiple refrigerators, endless computers and televisions etc., without efficient lifestyle changes. Eventually it will happen, but I don't think regular people paying 10-12¢ /kWh should jump on board. My electricity is cheap, yearly bill is only about $1,200 per year. I'm going to let the power companies mature this technology for me ;)
